name: Do I need to prime interior trim before painting it?

mainEntity.name: Do I need to prime interior trim before painting it?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need a dedicated primer if you are working with bare wood, transitioning from an oil-based finish to latex paint, or covering deep stains and knot holes. Previously painted latex trim in clean, sound condition often only requires scuff-sanding and a high-quality self-priming acrylic enamel. However, skipping primer on bare pine, patched nail holes, or slick surfaces leads to peeling paint and bleed-through. During on-site consultations, Abraham Becerra tests existing trim coatings with a quick solvent check to determine if an oil-to-acrylic bonding primer is necessary.
acceptedAnswer.description: Priming is required over bare wood, new drywall joints, stains, or old oil-based paint. Previously painted latex trim in good condition usually only needs cleaning and light sanding.
